evals.prompt: Reverse-engineer the requirements from the C program in code_repository/BasicGame.c. I want functional and non-functional requirements that are traceable back to the code. Put the output files in OUTDIR.
evals.expected_output: A requirements document (plus supporting analysis files) where every requirement cites a file/function/line, uses EARS phrasing, contains no invented numeric limits, reflects that seed() and getValidInteger() are never called, and includes a function-level traceability matrix.
assertions: Produced at least one markdown requirements document
Contains at least 10 requirement statements (shall/must)
At least 90% of requirement statements cite a source line number (and file, for multi-file inputs)
No weak/unmeasurable words in requirement statements
No requirements about the requirements document itself
Requirement statements do not embed function identifiers like foo()
No invented timing constraints (code has none)
Notes that seed() is never called / RNG is unseeded
Notes that getValidInteger() is never called
Captures the 200-point checkout end condition
Final document traces all 22 functions (each name appears)
Validated doc includes a traceability matrix section

evals.prompt: Generate a requirements spec for the Arduino sketch at Reports/Battery-Management-System-master/BMS.ino so a firmware engineer could re-implement it. Write the outputs to OUTDIR.
evals.expected_output: Requirements covering the SOC and SOH calculations with the actual formulas and constants (Ro, capacity), the analog pin reads, the delay-based timing, EEPROM persistence, pin/I2C constants as interface or constraint requirements, and explicit handling of BatteryManagement(), updates() and overcurrent() being defined but never called.
assertions: Produced at least one markdown requirements document
Contains at least 10 requirement statements (shall/must)
At least 90% of requirement statements cite a source line number (and file, for multi-file inputs)
No weak/unmeasurable words in requirement statements
No requirements about the requirements document itself
Requirement statements do not embed function identifiers like foo()
Notes BatteryManagement() is never called
Notes updates() is never called
Identifies overcurrent() as an interrupt handler
Captures capacity constant 4.5*3600 (16200 C)
Captures Ro = 1e-3
Captures I2C address 0x18 and pins 2 and 7
Captures the SOC formula (1 - Q/capacity)*100
Captures the 4.11 V SOH threshold
Captures EEPROM persistence of SOC, SOH, Q
Captures the 10000 ms delay in overcurrent()
